requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`. The YAML profile in `outline/languages/yaml.rs#const[KINDS]` has only three kinds, one for each construct in the requirement's table. They are `block_mapping_pair` and `flow_pair`, both a `pair` named by the written key, and `block_sequence_item`, an anonymous `item`.

- **Block mapping entries as `pair` with the written key.** `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs`) parses a YAML file and asserts the full summary. It expects `pair[a]`, `pair["b"]`, `pair[c]` and `pair[e]`. The quoted key is named as written, `pair["b"]`.
- **Flow mapping entries.** The same test has `c: {d: 1}` and expects `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d]`.
- **Block sequence entries as anonymous `item`.** The test has `e:` with a sequence `- f: 1` and `- 2`. It expects `item@` entries, one holding a mapping with its own pair and one a plain scalar. The two siblings are both `item@`, which shows the anonymous identity.
- **Nesting beneath the nearest enclosing item.** The expected summary is asserted exactly. The pair `f` sits under the `item@` under `pair[e]` under `pair["b"]`, and `pair[d]` sits under `pair[c]`. The summary also gives line spans such as 3-7 and 6-6.
- **Selected source ends at the last non-comment token.** `yaml_selection_ends_before_trailing_comment_tokens` (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`) covers three cases. In the first, `key: value # trailing comment` selects as `key: value`, with span 0..10. In the second, a comment line after a nested pair does not extend `pair[a]`, which selects as `a:\n  b: 1`. In the third, the nested `pair[a]/pair[b]` selects as `b: 1`.
- **Comment ownership.** This is delegated to the cited `requirements.references.outline_comments`. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` also checks a YAML comment line before a key. It expects the comment to belong to `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`.
- **Selector syntax, percent-encoding and duplicate suffixes.** These follow a cited requirement, so they are context here and need no test in this review.

Not tested: a trailing comment after a sequence item, and multi-entry flow mappings. The requirement does not single these out, and they go through the same generic mechanism as the covered cases. I do not count them as gaps.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
